what: Verified legal-AI adoption events in Saudi legal institutions, recorded as chronology and as future measurement anchors. NOT as evidence that any judgment was produced with AI, and NOT as evidence that any measured outcome moved.
correction: An earlier version of this file was empty, on the reasoning that nothing had been verified. That was wrong: it confused 'this repository has not looked' with 'nothing is verifiable'. A bounded search of official Saudi sources was run and seven events are recorded below. The empty registry made the AI-transition baseline look like a pre-adoption baseline. It is not one.
rules: An event is entered only with a citable source. Where our own fetch of that source was blocked, the block is recorded in fetch_status and the event's confirmed_status stays PENDING; a 403 or a 503 from our side is never treated as evidence that the source does not exist or does not say what it says.
AI exposure is NEVER inferred from the style, length, punctuation or fluency of a document. No detector output may be entered here, and no document in this corpus is or will be labelled AI-written.
An event describes an institution and a workflow, never an individual lawyer, judge or judgment.
A meeting, a workshop, a hackathon, a training programme or an award is not a deployment. deployment_status carries that distinction and it is never rounded up.
An event licenses an event-study window ONLY at corpus_linkability L3 or above. At L0, L1 or L2 it is chronology and nothing else.
verified_claims records what the source establishes. claims_not_established records what a reader might wrongly infer from it, and is mandatory.

schema.announcement_date: gregorian; UNKNOWN if the source does not date it
schema.institution_family: judiciary | administrative judiciary | ministry | regulator | data authority | vendor | professional body
schema.actor_channel: one of the seven channels in ai_transition_baseline_v2
schema.workflow_stage: legal research | drafting | document review | case triage | translation | retrieval | judicial administration | decision support | enforcement | public-facing legal assistance | governance
schema.technology_description: what the source says the system does
schema.deployment_status: DISCUSSION | TRAINING | PARTNERSHIP | PILOT | DEPLOYED | EXPANDED | PLANNED | GOVERNANCE | UNKNOWN
schema.users: who the source says uses it
schema.claims_not_established: what it does not establish, stated explicitly
schema.relation_to_baseline_cutoff: BEFORE | AFTER — the AI-transition baseline is frozen at 1446Q2, which ends approximately 31 December 2024
schema.measurement_opportunity: what, if anything, this repository could ever measure about it

baselineCutoffNote: The frozen AI-transition baseline has data cutoff 1446Q2. 1446Q2 runs approximately 4 October to 31 December 2024. Events dated before that are ALREADY INSIDE the baseline; events after it are outside. Three of the seven events below precede the cutoff.

adoptionThresholds.note: the observable conditions the conditional forecasts in FORECAST_LEDGER.json depend on. They were defined before any event was entered and are NOT revised now that events exist.
adoptionThresholds.T_RESEARCH_DEPLOYED: at least 3 events with confirmed_status CONFIRMED, source_quality OFFICIAL, workflow_stage in {legal research, retrieval}, actor_type in {court, ministry, regulator, legal research provider}, all dated before the forecast window
adoptionThresholds.T_DRAFTING_DEPLOYED: the same, with workflow_stage drafting and actor_type law firm, from at least 3 distinct organizations
adoptionThresholds.T_COURT_DECISION_SUPPORT: at least 1 CONFIRMED OFFICIAL event with actor_type court and workflow_stage in {decision support, judicial administration} and deployment_scope in {partial, institution-wide}

statusNow.T_RESEARCH_DEPLOYED: NOT MET as specified — the qualifying events are at the Board of Grievances, whose judgments are not in this corpus, and our own fetch of the SPA pages was blocked, so confirmed_status is PENDING rather than CONFIRMED
statusNow.T_DRAFTING_DEPLOYED: NOT MET — no verified law-firm deployment event was found
statusNow.T_COURT_DECISION_SUPPORT: ARGUABLY MET at the Board of Grievances (ADOPT-0002), NOT met at the Ministry of Justice commercial courts that this corpus observes

events.organization: SDAIA (Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority)
events.technology_description: Generative Artificial Intelligence Principles for Government Entities, first version, January 2024; later an AI Adoption Framework (2025) and an AI bias reference guide
events.verified_claims: a cross-government generative-AI principles document existed from January 2024 and is referenced by other government entities' own AI policies
events.claims_not_established: that any court, ministry or law firm deployed anything. A principles document governs use; it does not evidence use in any particular institution.
events.measurement_opportunity: none directly. It dates the start of a governed adoption period and is the anchor other events cite.
events.notes: entered because the Board of Grievances AI-principles document cites it by name and version, which is how it was found.

events.technology_description: the «مساعد» (Musaed) knowledge-assistant programme: a data-sharing agreement to use an intelligent knowledge assistant for searching judicial precedents and current legislation, described in the reporting as extending to prediction of the judicial ruling
events.users: Board of Grievances judges and researchers, per the reporting
events.verified_claims: a system named ALMUSAID is hosted on an official Board of Grievances subdomain, so a production system of that name exists; a cooperation agreement between the Board and Elm covering it was reported by Saudi press
events.claims_not_established: how many judges use it, how often, on which case types, or whether the described prediction functionality was ever enabled. Our own fetch of the system returned a title only, and the prediction claim comes from press reporting rather than from a Board publication we could read.
events.measurement_opportunity: the Board of Grievances publishes administrative judgments in its own collection, which is NOT in this corpus. Measuring this event would require that collection, which is outside the current source and outside the standing scope.
events.notes: this is the single most important entry in the file: a judicial legal-research AI in a Saudi court, dated BEFORE the frozen baseline. It is also in the wrong judiciary for this corpus to observe.

events.technology_description: the knowledge assistant (المساعد المعرفي) placed among the top five in the Digital Government Award 2024 for best use of emerging technologies, described as using AI over precedent, procedure and legislation data to return organised information and recommendations
events.verified_claims: the system was in a state mature enough to be entered for, and recognised in, a national digital-government award during 2024
events.claims_not_established: that it changed any judicial output. An award recognises a system, not an effect.
events.measurement_opportunity: same as ADOPT-0002: the affected corpus is the Board's own, not this one.
events.notes: recorded separately from ADOPT-0002 because an agreement and a working awarded system are different facts with different dates.

events.technology_description: the Virtual Enforcement Court: on the Ministry's own page, enforcement requests are completed from filing to the issuance and service of decisions automatically and without human intervention, under direct judicial supervision. Press and SPA material additionally describe AI enablers, automatic classification of enforcement requests, electronic verification of instruments and data analysis for anticipating problems.
events.verified_claims: the Ministry states the court is launched and that enforcement procedures run automatically without human intervention under judicial supervision
events.claims_not_established: THE MINISTRY'S OWN PAGE DOES NOT MENTION ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE. Automation without human intervention is not evidence of machine learning. The AI enablers, classification and prediction language comes from press and agency material, not from the page we read. And nothing here touches judicial reasoning in commercial adjudication, which is what this corpus measures.
events.measurement_opportunity: enforcement workflow outcomes, which this corpus does not carry. It is L2 and not L3: same ministry, different workflow, different published output.
events.notes: the clearest example in the file of why deployment_status and corpus_linkability must be recorded separately. A real, institution-wide, official deployment that this repository cannot measure at all.

events.technology_description: Principles for the Use of Artificial Intelligence Systems: a binding internal document applying to every Board department and to operating companies that use, build or operate AI systems at any stage of their life cycle, with compliance monitored by the Governance and Risk Management administration, citing SDAIA's Generative AI Principles for Government Entities (first version, January 2024)
events.users: all Board of Grievances personnel using AI systems
events.verified_claims: the Board issued a mandatory internal AI-use policy. A policy addressed to personnel who use AI systems is evidence that AI systems are in use across the institution, which is a stronger fact than any single product announcement.
events.claims_not_established: which systems, in which chambers, at what volume, or with what effect on judgments.
events.measurement_opportunity: none in this corpus. It dates the point at which institutional AI use became governed rather than experimental.
events.notes: issued alongside the Cabinet's designation of 2026 as a year of artificial intelligence, per the reporting.

events.technology_description: a cooperation agreement to develop the administrative enforcement platform (منصة التنفيذ الإدارية) and to expand the use of AI and data analysis in administrative-judiciary work
events.verified_claims: an administrative enforcement platform exists on the Board's own e-services, and a cooperation agreement to develop it further with AI and data analysis was reported
events.claims_not_established: that any AI component of that platform is live, or what it does
events.notes: a partnership, not a deployment. Recorded so that a future deployment announcement has a predecessor to be dated against.

events.technology_description: the President of the Board received a delegation from HUMAIN, a PIF artificial-intelligence company, to explore developing digital and intelligent solutions for judicial and administrative work
events.verified_claims: a meeting took place and opportunities were reviewed
events.claims_not_established: everything else. No system, no pilot, no scope, no users. This is the entry that most needs its status kept honest, and it is entered at DISCUSSION for exactly that reason.
events.notes: our own fetch of the SPA page returned 403. That is our access failing, not the source failing; the URL and its content summary are recorded and confirmed_status stays PENDING.

notFound: No verified deployment event was found for the Saudi Bar Association or for any named Saudi law firm. The ADVOCACY channel is therefore NO_VERIFIED_EVENT in this registry, which is a statement about our search, not about Saudi legal practice.

No verified AI deployment event was found for the Ministry of Justice COMMERCIAL courts, whose judgments are this corpus. Every event that touches a court in this registry touches the Board of Grievances or MoJ enforcement.
searchScope: Bounded search, run once, of SPA, Board of Grievances, Ministry of Justice, SDAIA and Digital Government Authority material plus Saudi press reporting that names them. Not a news archive and not maintained continuously. Absence from this file means we did not verify it, never that it does not exist.
